Capitalism may be a large reason for depression

The victim of a crime is the second worst person to ask what punishment a criminal should receive. The worst is the criminal.

The purpose of pursuing justice is to metaphorically level the scales. This requires a dispassionate and impartial arbiter that has nothing to gain/lose from the outcome. Without an impartial arbiter handing out the sentences the criminal justice system would eventually become a cycle of blackmail, intimidation, and revenge.

No - it would not lower the crime rate in general, because:

a) many "personal" crimes are crimes of passion (not pre-mediated, in the moment, unplanned)

b) many "victimless" crimes are risk based, noting that nothing in terms of penalty counts if you get away with it.

c) many crimes are (property crimes in particular) addiction or needs based - they will happen regardless of penalty because they haven't addressed the symptoms (drug addition for instance).

d) organised crime is organised crime and has a large victim base or is victim-less - you're assuming only one wronged party here.
It would likely have no discernible effect on the crime rate, but it just might make our criminal justice system even more broken then it already is.
